marks.gloss_en: כדאמר רב פפא: במרודד, הכא נמי במרודד (= p_okimta_merudad)
here too, [R' Yochanan speaks] of [flesh that is] meruddad
Rav Pappa: [the mishna speaks of flesh that is] meruddad
במרודד (= p_rav_pappa_bimrudad)
רבי דוסא בן הרכינס -- דתנן ... (124b.5), and לאו אמר רבי דוסא התם אין מאהיל וחוזר ומאהיל, הכא נמי אין נוגע וחוזר ונוגע (124b.6)
all that impart impurity in a tent which were divided and one brought them into a house -- R' Dosa ben Harkinas declares pure
כדקתני סיפא: ומודה רבי עקיבא בשני חצאי זיתים שתחבן בקיסם והסיטן שהוא טמא
ומפני מה רבי עקיבא מטהר בעור? מפני שהעור מבטלן
R' Akiva purifies only with the hide; elsewhere he renders impure, as the seifa teaches (= p_ra_bealma_metamei)
R' Akiva purifies only with the hide; elsewhere he renders impure
מאי טעמא? כתיב ונשא וקרינן נושא -- בעינן נושא והוא דנישא בבת אחת
it is written 'venisa' and we read 'nosei': we require 'nosei' and that it be 'nisa' [carried] at once
ומדרבי דוסא כרבי ישמעאל, רבנן כרבי עקיבא? והא רבי עקיבא טהורי קא מטהר! -- the Sages of Oholot render impure, but R' Akiva [who denies even carrying] purifies
מתיב: the baraita has R' Akiva deny carrying because it does not come under contact -- ואם איתא, הרי בא לכלל מגע מלפניו (124b.11): if Bar Padda is right, it does come under contact from the front
'their carcass' (Lev 11) -- and not a hide on which there are two half-olive-bulks
הכי קאמר: what comes under contact IN EVERY WAY comes under carrying (= p_rava_bechol_tzad)
Rava: this is what he says: what comes under contact in every way comes under carrying; what does not come under contact in every way does not
תנן: two half-olives on the hide impart impurity by carrying -- R' Yishmael. אמאי? והא לאו נישא הוא!
תא שמע: R' Akiva concedes [two half-olives] skewered on a chip and moved -- impure. אמאי? והא לאו נישא הוא!
הכי נמי במרודד (= p_modeh_bimrudad)
here too, [R' Akiva's concession speaks of flesh that is] meruddad
אטו נושא לאו מסיט הוא? -- 'even the carrier' adds nothing, for a carrier is one who moves
the baraita: both one who touches and one who moves [are impure]
אלא לאו הכי קאמר: touching and moving without nisa; R' Eliezer comes to say: provided it is nisa. [Attack on this answer, not representable:] ומאי אף? -- אימא: והוא דנישא
[on the stam's reading] the tanna kamma: touching and moving [render impure] without 'nisa'
Bar Padda: they taught [R' Yishmael's 'not by contact'] only from behind it
R' Yochanan: R' Yishmael and R' Dosa ben Harkinas said one thing
overshadowing and overshadowing again [joins]
might it be even by carrying? the verse says: 'and the carrier shall be impure'
a sealed thigh-bone, according to R' Yishmael -- what is [the law], does it impart impurity?
does R' Yishmael hold 'what comes under contact comes under carrying', and here [the two half-olives] the reason is that it comes under contact from the front? -- or perhaps he does not hold it?
Rabba bar Rav Huna said to him: a raven flew
Rava his son: isn't this Rav Avya Sava of Pumbedita, of whom the Master tells us in praise that he is a great man?
Ulla: two half-olive-bulks skewered on a wood chip -- even if one carries them to and fro all day, he is pure
